title: Indian States and Capitals Made Memorable
summary: Tricks to remember capitals and a quick tour of India's regions.

steps.title: A big country
sentences: India has 28 states and 8 union territories.
The capital of India is New Delhi.
Each state has its own capital, language and traditions.

steps.title: The south
sentences: Tamil Nadu's capital is Chennai, Kerala's is Thiruvananthapuram, and Karnataka's is Bengaluru.
Puducherry is a union territory in the south, and its capital has the same name.

steps.title: Memory tricks
sentences: Link each place with a picture or a story you will remember.
Break long names into small parts, for example Thi-ru-va-nan-tha-pu-ram, and say them slowly.
Learn in groups: states that share a border, one region at a time, and draw a rough map as you go.
points: Learn by region and draw a map

steps.title: Languages and cultures
sentences: India has 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, and hundreds more are spoken.
Each region has its own food, music, dance and festivals.
Learning about them is a good way to understand our unity in diversity.

facts: The smallest Indian state by area is Goa.
The largest state by area is Rajasthan.
Telangana, formed in 2014, is the newest of India's states.

quiz.q: What is the capital of Karnataka?
quiz.why: Bengaluru is the capital of Karnataka.

quiz.q: What is the capital of India?
Which state is the largest by area?
quiz.why: Rajasthan is the largest state by area.

notes: The number of states and union territories can change if Parliament changes them. Check an official source for the latest.
